subject: RE: Discovery — Prompt collection & model fit follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Discovery — Prompt collection & model fit follow-up

Hi Sam — great talking earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery focused on model fit, evals, and collecting prompts for quality checks: 

1) Recommended models to try (based on your latency and cost targets):
   - rw-13b-v1 (best quality / good for long-form rewriting)
   - rw-7b-q4_0 (cost-efficient, strong for Q&A and routing)
   - rw-3b-fast (low-latency option for synchronous UX)

2) Benchmarks and prompt sets
   - I attached a prompt_set_template.csv you can use to drop in representative customer prompts, edge cases, and expected outputs.
   - We’ll run a baseline eval against rw-13b-v1 and rw-7b-q4_0 and share token-cost + latency tradeoffs.
   - Benchmark sheet link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cBenchmarkSheet

3) Quality & regression concerns
   - We’ll baseline current performance and set a regression threshold (e.g., 5% drop in pass-rate on your key prompts).
   - We recommend adding at least 50 high-priority prompts and 20 edge-case/redaction-sensitive prompts so we can surface regressions tied to prompt variants.

4) Redaction guidance / PII
   - See attached redaction_guidelines.pdf for our recommended redaction patterns (order numbers, SSNs, emails). If you need us to run a sanitized-redaction pass we can do that as part of eval prep.

5) Next steps / timeline
   - Sam: drop sample prompts and any edge-case notes into the attached CSV by end of next week (Dec 8).
   - Redwood: we’ll run a first-pass eval within 3 business days of receiving prompts and get back a model recommendation + short report.
   - Optional: schedule a 30-min prompt collection call; happy to join and help classify prompts live.

Attachments: prompt_set_template.csv, redaction_guidelines.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the prompt set.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference — production-first inference for LLMs
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: RE: Discovery — Prompt collection & model fit follow-up

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. I dropped three sample prompts below to get us started; I’ll fill the CSV with more by EOW. A couple quick questions inline.

1) Sample prompts (real customer phrasing)
- "What's the status of order #ORD-992827?"
- "Can you summarize the last three interactions we had with Acme support on billing?"
- "We need an executive summary of usage trends for Q3 for our board deck."

2) Redaction question
- For order numbers like ORD-992827, do you prefer we redact in the CSV (e.g., ORD-REDACT) or include real values and mark them as PII? We want the evals to reflect production formats but avoid sharing real customer identifiers.

If it helps, we can schedule that 30-min prompt collection call next Tuesday morning.

Thanks,
Sam

Looping in some quick notes from the evaluation side:

- When you drop prompts into the CSV, please add a column for expected_output (short text) and a "priority" tag (P0/P1/P2). That helps us prioritize which prompts to include in the regression monitor.
- For redaction, safest approach for eval accuracy is: include a realistic token-length placeholder (e.g., ORD-XXXXX or <ORDER_ID>) rather than full real identifiers. Mark a separate column "pii=true" so we know which entries should be tested for redaction-aware behavior.
- We’ll seed the initial eval set with the 50 highest-priority prompts you provide, run against rw-13b-v1 and rw-7b-q4_0, and produce: pass/fail matrix, avg latency (p95), and per-prompt examples showing differences.

Ben
